correctness.rationale: The sampling distribution has active-coordinate probability s/d and Dirichlet(1) face weights, giving Gram diagonal 2/[d(s+1)] and kernel 1+[d(s+1)/2]x dot y. Convexity and strict sign disagreement localize all maximizing evaluations at vertices. The vertex integral reduces exactly to the positive part of a signed Beta(1,s-1) marginal, giving the closed norm. A derivative inequality proves strict rank monotonicity; second-order Taylor estimates give the uniform 1/d error band. These analytic identities prove all ranges; 1984 exact checker assertions confirm finite instances and independent polynomial beta integrals.

value.rationale: The object is the entire natural hierarchy of Hausdorff sampling measures on cross-polytope faces, and the precise invariant is worst-case Lp endpoint amplification for affine least squares. The sharp all-intermediate-rank profile, localization, strict rank monotonicity and a uniform quantitative dimension/rank band answer a non-implied stability question; it is neither an arbitrary low-dimensional table nor a parameter renaming. The mathematical value is the complete exact invariant and shape/rank interpretation; no downstream theorem is asserted.
